notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg2583.tlg001.1st1K-gr: Hermes and Zeus are the planets Mercury and Jupiter; 'terms' (ὅροι) are the astrological bounds into which each sign is divided.

Ares, Zeus and Cronus are the planets Mars, Jupiter and Saturn; the 'lurking' (φωλεύοντα) signs are a class of zodiac signs; 'below the earth' is the lower angle of the chart. 'Men who court danger' (παραβαλλομένους) may mean snake-handlers. The masculine προκαλοῦντος does not agree with the feminine viper.

nodes.text: they became seers, astronomers and augurs,
prophesying to mortals from entrails and from burnt offerings,
or magi, calling the gods with unspeakable songs.
But if Hermes should be in the terms of Zeus, and in turn in those of Hermes
that one [Zeus], and they look upon each other with friendly rays,
lifting a sharp sword in their palms to the sound of drums,
they imitate the accursed, god-possessed Attis of Cybele.
But if Ares, having the angles in the lurking signs
shared with Zeus, should look upon Cronus when he is below the earth,
he makes root-cutters, men who court danger, enchanters,
seeking an ill-starred death, and likewise the doom
of the dread-raging, broad-necked asp, and of the viper,
the blood-devouring *dipsas* [thirst-snake], which summons a fearful death
with a Tantalean punishment, as beneath its jaws, with its teeth,
it belches out thirst-bringing venom with a terrible breath.
